items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: Red Allen and Greely [Walton] and Barney Bigard and Albert Nicholas, all those guys were scattered, that's obvious. And they joined that band...

ctx.x: I give you the idea who I worked with then - I mean, that'll help you out too, see. Why I say you can't always go by the books, I mean because Hugues Panassie had Barney Bigard makin' 'Aunt Hagar's Blues'. And I made it, not only did I make the record, I made the arrangement for Clarence Williams, see what I'm talkin' about?

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: And the guy next to me, his name was Benny Waters... Benny Waters said, 'Have you met him?' I said, 'No, who is he?' He said, 'That's Benny Carter.'

ctx.x:
See, when I worked at the Nest with Luis Russell, well, that was Charlie Johnson's band -- that was his second band. He booked Luis in there, see? And when I worked with -- Charlie wanted me to come in his band, the big band, like the mother band, as you would say, and I didn't want to leave Luis. So then I'd go there sometime and sit in, you know.

So the funny part about the night I went to sit in, I wanted to meet this -- I heard so much about this Benny Carter so much I wanted to meet him and hear him play.…

Benny Waters said, "Have you met him?" I said, "No, who is he?" He said, "That's Benny Carter." I said, "Oh, it is." Boy, I felt about that low, you know. And he had finished that arrangement, so I put my horn away and went to sit down and listen, and when I heard I walked out.
